title: policy transparency endpoint and kms pseudonymization adapter
author: Anya Patel
release_notes: Added a feature-flagged Policy Transparency endpoint that serves signed, pseudonymized policy/audit exports for certified auditors and compliance owners. Introduces a KMS pseudonymization adapter and RBAC v2 policy exporter. Backwards-compatible and feature-flag gated.
description: Motivation: Customers and auditors increasingly ask for exported proofs of access and policy state that do not leak tenant PII or raw key material. Current audit exports are rich but contain operator identifiers and exact key ARNs that some customers cannot share with external auditors. This PR introduces a feature-flagged Policy Transparency endpoint (GET /internal/compliance/policy-transparency) which returns a signed bundle containing: a diff of RBAC v2 policies (human- and machine-readable), KMS usage summaries with pseudonymized key identifiers (via the new KMS Pseudonymization Adapter), and an attestable audit log slice (time-windowed) where sensitive fields are redacted or replaced with stable pseudonyms. Design highlights: - KMS Pseudonymization Adapter: a pluggable layer in the key-usage exporter that replaces exact key ids with deterministic pseudonyms per-tenant + per-audit-session salt. Pseudonyms are stable within an audit run but irreversible without the session salt, which is exposed only to the auditor via a short-lived, auditable grant. - RBAC v2 exporter: walks the policy store, computes normalized diffs between the requested window and the prior snapshot, and includes policy fingerprints and human-readable rationale fields. - Signed bundles: bundles are signed with the compliance service key (stored in KMS) and include a hash manifest so downstream verification is trivial. - Feature gating: exposed under feature gate policy_transparency_v1 and an RBAC guard requiring org:compliance-reader role. - Privacy controls: default export redacts operator emails and replaces them with stable pseudonyms; optional pseudonym reveal is gated by an explicit auditor grant backed by SUP-8841 workflow. Checklist: - [x] Adapter for pseudonymization added and unit-tested - [x] RBAC v2 exporter implemented with diff & fingerprinting - [x] Signed bundle format defined and documented (docs/internal/compliance) - [x] Feature flag + rollout plan (5% beta, org opt-in) - [x] E2E test exercising signer and verification flow - [x] Security review and threat model updated Context and scope: This PR does not change actual KMS key usage, key policy enforcement, or tenant key scoping. It only transforms what is present in exported artifacts and adds an access-controlled endpoint for compliance. The session-salt reveal mechanism is implemented in a companion PR for the auditor-access service (SUP-8841) and is intentionally separate to keep the data-plane export immutable and verifiable. Commits summary: - Add KMS pseudonymization adapter and deterministic pseudonym generator - Implement RBAC v2 policy walker and diff engine - Add bundle signer + verification helpers - Hook endpoint into compliance service with RBAC guard and feature gate - Add e2e tests and integration test harness updates - Documentation: internal spec and migration notes Changed files (high level): - services/compliance/api.go (new endpoint + handler) - services/compliance/exporter/pseudonym_adapter.go (new) - services/compliance/exporter/pseudonym_test.go (unit tests) - services/compliance/exporter/pseudonym_impl.go (deterministic salt logic) - core/rbac/exporter/exporter.go (policy walker + diff engine) - core/rbac/exporter/serializer.go (fingerprint + human readable output) - infra/iam/roles.yaml (new org:compliance-reader role) - docs/internal/compliance/policy-transparency.md (spec) - tests/e2e/compliance_transparency_test.go - build/ci/compliance_exporter_pipeline.yml - pkg/crypto/signature.go (bundle signer helpers) - scripts/rollout/feature_flag_policy_transparency.sh Review conversation (selected): - Marcus Li (reviewer): "This looks comprehensive. Two concerns: 1) the deterministic pseudonym generator — how do we handle key rotation on the backend KMS? Could the pseudonym map break when a key is replaced? 2) performance when exporting a large window (multi-day)." - Author (Anya): "Answers: 1) pseudonymization operates on key fingerprint (SHA256 over key public metadata + key-id). When a key is rotated, the fingerprint changes and the pseudonym will change — which is intended (the export will show a different pseudonym, and the diff engine will surface that as key-rotation). For stable cross-window mapping we also include an optional 'alias hint' field that points to tenant-provided aliases if available. 2) Export path is stream-processed; we implemented a streaming serializer and the exporter supports chunked signatures to avoid OOMs. Benchmarks in tests show 2x memory reduction vs naive buffering." - Sofia Morales (reviewer): "Please add a note to the threat model about an attacker who obtains a session salt. What mitigations exist?" - Author (Anya): "Added threat model section and an auditor-secret TTL + KYC gating note. Session salts are short lived, logged to the auditor grant ledger, and we rotate the grant after use (see docs)." - Devon Harris (approver): "Approve after nits: make the feature-flag default off and add a metrics counter for exports per org." - Anya: "Addressed: feature flag defaults to off, plus export_counter{org} metric added and linked to Console dashboard." CI summary: - unit tests: pass - integration tests: pass (compliance exporter harness) - lint: pass with minor golint warnings fixed in subsequent commit - security scan: pass with low-severity findings (noted in PR) Merge outcome: merged via squash on 2026-03-01 by repository maintainers. Post-merge actions: - Rollout plan in docs/ops/rollouts.md (staged 5% -> 50% -> org opt-in) - Follow-up PRs: auditor-access grant flow (SUP-8841) and console UI for granting reveal (ENG-9278) Monitoring and observability: - export_counter{org} metric added - bundle_sign_latency histogram - compliance_export_errors counter - dashboard and alert runbook added under observability/compliance Export privacy guarantees (short): - Raw KMS key IDs are never present in exported bundles unless an auditor grant reveals them. - Pseudonyms are deterministic per-session and tenant and are irreversible without the session salt. - Signed bundles allow auditors to verify the integrity of exports without relying on live access. Operational notes: - Because the bundles are signed with the compliance service KMS key, rotation of that key will result in new signatures; we include signer-key-id in the manifest so auditors can verify previous bundle signatures against archived signer keys. - Feature gate controlled: disable quickly via feature flag if unexpected privacy concerns appear. Documentation: docs/internal/compliance/policy-transparency.md contains API schema, bundle format, threat model, rollout steps, and verification example. Migration: No customer migration required; org admins must opt in to enable exports. Known limitations: - Pseudonym reveal workflow is out-of-band (separate PR) - Very large exports can still be slow; we recommend limiting window to 7 days for initial rollout.
